questions.stem: Which part of the brain acts as the body's thermostat, monitoring blood temperature?

options.text: The medulla oblongata
The cerebrum
The cerebellum
The hypothalamus

questions.explanation: The hypothalamus contains the thermoregulatory centre that monitors blood temperature. It has receptors that detect changes in blood temperature and triggers appropriate responses to maintain body temperature at around 37 degrees C.

questions.stem: When body temperature rises too high, what happens to blood vessels in the skin?

options.text: They close completely to prevent blood flow
They constrict (vasoconstriction) to trap heat
They dilate (vasodilation) to release more heat
They remain unchanged

questions.explanation: When the body is too hot, blood vessels near the skin surface dilate (vasodilation). This increases blood flow near the surface, allowing more heat to be lost to the environment by radiation, helping to cool the body down.

questions.stem: How does sweating help to cool the body?

options.text: Sweat blocks sunlight from reaching the skin
Cold sweat absorbs heat from the skin
Sweat cools the blood directly as it passes through sweat glands
Sweat evaporates from the skin, taking heat energy with it

questions.explanation: When sweat evaporates from the skin surface, it absorbs heat energy (latent heat of vaporisation) from the body. This transfer of heat energy into the evaporating sweat cools the skin and the blood flowing beneath it.

questions.stem: What happens when the body is too cold?

options.text: Hair follicles relax and hairs lie flat
Blood vessels in the skin dilate
Sweat glands produce more sweat
Muscles contract rapidly (shivering) to generate heat

questions.explanation: When the body is too cold, skeletal muscles contract and relax rapidly (shivering). This involuntary movement requires energy from respiration, and the heat released as a by-product helps to warm the body.

questions.stem: Why is it important to maintain body temperature at approximately 37 degrees C?

options.text: Because blood cannot flow at other temperatures
Because this is the optimum temperature for enzyme activity
Because the heart can only beat at this temperature
Because water freezes below this temperature

questions.explanation: 37 degrees C is the optimum temperature for human enzyme activity. At this temperature, enzymes work most efficiently. If temperature rises too high, enzymes denature; if it drops too low, enzyme activity decreases significantly.

options.text: The narrowing of blood vessels near the skin to reduce heat loss
The production of sweat by sweat glands
The widening of blood vessels to increase heat loss
The contraction of muscles during shivering

questions.explanation: Vasoconstriction is the narrowing of blood vessels near the skin surface. This reduces blood flow to the skin, meaning less heat is lost by radiation to the environment. It is a response to the body being too cold.

questions.stem: Temperature regulation is controlled by which type of feedback?

options.text: Positive feedback
No feedback is involved
Chemical feedback only
Negative feedback

questions.explanation: Temperature regulation uses negative feedback. When body temperature rises above the set point, cooling mechanisms are activated. When it falls below, warming mechanisms are activated. In both cases, the response counteracts the change.
